testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is aggressive driving?

options.text: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
Driving with concern for other drivers' safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means operating a vehicle in a selfish or pushy way with no regard for the safety of other road users.

questions.question: A fire extinguisher is a required piece of safety equipment.
questions.explanation: When you inspect a vehicle, you must check for required emergency equipment. This includes at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
It ensures the vehicle is inspected regularly.
It keeps drivers responsible for inspecting their vehicles.
It provides a plan for the next five trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report lets the driver inform the motor carrier of issues that could affect safe operation. Drivers should complete this report after each day of driving. Note any issues that could affect vehicle safety or cause a mechanical breakdown.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Usually happens when traveling above 65 mph.
Can happen with just a little water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen with just a little water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when a vehicle's tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. You do not need a large amount of water for this to happen. Hydroplaning can start at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: A cargo cover that flaps while you drive:

options.text: Allows air to cool the cargo.

questions.explanation: Cargo covers should not flap in the wind. A flapping cover can tear off completely, exposing your cargo and blocking your view or other drivers' views.

questions.question: When driving long distances, you should:
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, take a break after every 100 miles or every 2 hours of driving. Driving through the night or when you would normally sleep increases the risk of fatigue.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is always dangerous because the driver may not see everything behind them. CMV drivers should avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: The faster you drive:

options.text: The shorter your stopping distance will be.
The longer your stopping distance will be.
The easier it will be to stop your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer your stopping distance will be.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop your vehicle. Brake as needed based on your speed.

questions.question: Cargo inside a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured.
Should be stacked no higher than three feet.
Should be secured to prevent it from moving.
Should be loaded with the heaviest items on top.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be secured to prevent it from moving.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured properly to prevent movement while traveling. Arrange cargo to keep the vehicle's center of gravity low and balanced.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation in your personal car:

options.text: Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.explanation: If you are convicted of any traffic violation while driving any vehicle, you must notify your employer within 30 days. Parking violations are not included in this rule.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: Rain mixes with oil on the road.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil that has dripped onto the road. This mixture is very slippery and dangerous.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Use the parking brake every time you park your vehicle.

questions.question: Is a broken exhaust system safe?
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous. Toxic fumes can enter the cab or sleeper area.

questions.question: What type of air brake system do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems with one set of controls.

questions.question: What should you do when turning?

options.text: Turn off your turn signal just before starting the turn.
Signal only if vehicles are in front of you.

questions.explanation: Turn on your signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep the signal on during the turn. Turn it off after you complete the turn if your vehicle doesn't turn it off automatically.

questions.question: If your personal driving license is suspended or revoked, can you get a hardship license to drive a commercial vehicle?

options.text: Yes, you can get a hardship license.
No, you cannot get a hardship license.
Your commercial license will not be affected.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you cannot get a hardship license.
questions.explanation: If your personal driving license is suspended, canceled, or revoked, you cannot get a hardship license to drive a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: What does ABS do?

options.text: Prevents front brakes from working on ice.
Stops brakes from being used if downshifting works better.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops wheels from locking up when you brake hard, especially on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS is not working?

options.text: Brake normally. Your brakes still work.
Press the brake pedal as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally. Your brakes still work.
questions.explanation: Without a working ABS, your vehicle still has normal brakes. Brake as you normally would. Get your ABS repaired as soon as possible.

questions.question: When should you learn the controls of a new vehicle?
questions.explanation: Learn how to use all the controls and features of a new vehicle before you drive it.

questions.question: What are air tank drains used for?

options.text: They let rain water into the tank.
They remove water and oil from the tank.
They must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the tank.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks need to be drained to remove water and oil that build up. This must be done to prevent damage. Use manual drains at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: When driving, your mirrors should:

options.text: Not be used because they distract you.
Not be used unless there is traffic.

questions.explanation: You need to know what is around you at all times. Check your mirrors regularly.

questions.question: A second conviction for driving a CMV with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.04 percent or higher will result in:

options.text: Loss of your CDL for life.
Loss of your CDL for five years.
Loss of your CDL for one year.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of your CDL for life.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive a CMV with a BAC of 0.04 percent or higher. A first offense costs you your CDL for one year. A second offense costs you your CDL for life.

questions.question: When turning, when should you turn off your turn signal?

options.text: In the middle of the turn

questions.explanation: Signal early and keep signaling while turning or changing lanes. Turn off your signal after the turn or lane change is done.

questions.question: A vehicle smaller than yours:

options.text: Can usually stop faster than your vehicle.
Usually takes longer to stop than your vehicle.
Takes about the same time to stop as your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can usually stop faster than your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles can stop faster than larger vehicles. Remember this when deciding how far back to follow other cars.

questions.question: If you get a traffic violation in your personal car:

options.text: The officer will tell your employer.
Your CDL will not be affected because it happened in your personal car.
You should tell your employer within six months.
You must tell your employer within 30 days.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer within 30 days.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction in any vehicle. Parking violations do not count.

questions.question: What color are ABS warning lamps?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lamps.

questions.question: To use controlled braking, you should:

options.text: Brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing your brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels. Keep steering movements small while using this method.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is normal when a vehicle is warmed up.

questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually so the vehicle does not jerk. Rough acceleration can harm the vehicle's engine and parts.

questions.question: A 10-foot load needs at least ____ tie-down(s).
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers and open trailers must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: If you see a construction worker near the road while driving slowly through a construction zone, you should:
questions.explanation: Always drive slowly in construction areas. Slow down further if workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: What may prevent someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) considers them a security threat.
They are a lawful U.S. citizen.
They work for a foreign company.
They do not have perfect vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) considers them a security threat.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if you renounce your U.S. citizenship, are not a lawful permanent U.S. resident, are wanted for or convicted of certain felonies, are judged mentally defective, are committed to a mental institution, or if the TSA believes you pose a security threat.

questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Should take over-the-counter medicines to stay awake.
May make important decisions too slowly.
Is usually more careful than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: May make important decisions too slowly.
questions.explanation: Tired drivers cannot see or react to dangers as quickly. They have trouble making important decisions.

questions.question: Good drivers look ____ seconds ahead of their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors to guide you.
Walk around first to check for obstacles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around first to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Walk around your vehicle before backing to look for obstacles. Mirrors have blind spots, so you cannot depend on them alone. Use a helper when possible.

questions.question: When an engine is running, good oil pressure would be:
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should be between 35 and 75 psi. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or changing.

questions.question: Regrooved tires are allowed:

options.text: Only on the front of a bus.
Only on the rear of a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only on the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front of a bus.

questions.question: Using a hands-free phone while driving:

options.text: Only distracts the driver when speaking.

questions.explanation: Hands-free phones are safer than hand-held phones, but they can still distract you mentally. Any conversation takes your focus away from driving.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens most often when:

options.text: A vehicle is traveling faster than 60 mph.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely when driving on wet roads with low tire pressure and worn tread. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: What could reduce clearance between the road and an overhead object like a bridge?
questions.explanation: Do not assume bridge height signs are always correct. If the road was repaved after the sign was posted, or if snow is on the ground, the clearance may be different.

questions.question: If you must drive slowly and block other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you if you must drive slowly (if local laws allow).

questions.question: Exercise will help a person sober up after drinking.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol from your body at a fixed rate. Exercise, cold showers, and other tricks will not speed this up. The only way to sober up is to wait for your body to process the alcohol.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you will be evaluated on lane usage. Which is an example of poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Driving in the leftmost lane when more than one lane is available
Finishing a right turn in the rightmost lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in the leftmost lane when more than one lane is available
questions.explanation: During the on-road test, do not drive over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines and crosswalks. On roads with multiple lanes, finish turns in the correct lane. Stay in the rightmost lane unless it is blocked.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle controls test, your vehicle's final position should be:

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be in the exact position the examiner described when you finish each exercise. If you do not complete an exercise exactly as directed, you may fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: Who is responsible for inspecting a vehicle's cargo?

options.text: The owner of the trucking company

questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for inspecting cargo. This includes checking for overloading, poor weight balance, and proper securing. The driver must make sure cargo does not block their view or block access to emergency equipment. The driver is always responsible for their cargo, even if someone else loaded it.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air pressure pushes out the rod and moves the:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops the compressor from pumping air once the air tanks reach:
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when the air tanks reach 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: When stopping, the brake pedal should be:

options.text: Pressed down quickly with both feet.

questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down gradually for a smooth, safe stop.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid level in some vehicles, the vehicle:

options.text: May need to be left running.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to be left running.
questions.explanation: For some vehicles, you may need to leave the engine running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: Heavy steering is often a sign of:
questions.explanation: Heavy steering usually means one of your front tires has failed. If steering feels different, pull off the road safely and check your tires.

questions.question: One way to avoid becoming an aggressive driver is to:

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Set realistic expectations about travel time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set realistic expectations about travel time.
questions.explanation: To avoid frustration and aggressive driving, plan ahead and allow extra time for traffic delays. Other ways to prevent aggressive driving include driving at a safe speed, maintaining a safe following distance, avoiding rude gestures, and keeping both hands on the wheel.
